transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

For years now I’ve felt this constant heaviness and sadness that never really lifts, even when things in my life are going okay. It just feels like a persistent weight I can't seem to shake off, no matter how hard I try to keep moving forward.
How long have you been feeling this heaviness and sadness? Has it been present most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks or longer?

It has been hanging over me steadily for a little over three years now, starting around the time my husband and I separated. It is much more than just a couple of weeks; it is there most days, feeling like a constant lead blanket or a dull, heavy sadness in my chest that never really lets up.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["F32.1", "F32.2", "F34.1"], but based on this conversation, F32.1 (moderate depressive episode) and F32.2 (severe depressive episode without psychotic symptoms) are less likely because the patient describes a chronic, persistent low mood lasting over three years with no mention of episodic major depression or acute worsening typical of major depressive episodes. Instead, the long duration, early onset after a stressor, and persistent but relatively stable nature of the symptoms align more closely with F34.1 (dysthymia). Therefore, the current candidate is F34.1.

This pattern is consistent with dysthymia (F34.1) or a persistent depressive disorder. However, since the patient mentions this occurs even when life circumstances are stable or positive, and given the duration and severity, major depressive disorder (single episode, mild F32.1 or moderate/severe F32.2) must also be considered. At this stage, the differential includes both persistent depressive disorder and major depression, as insufficient detail exists to rule out either.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a chronic, low-grade depressed mood lasting for over three years, with onset following a psychosocial stressor (marital separation), meeting the duration and symptom criteria for dysthymia (persistent depressive disorder). There is no indication of acute major depressive episode, but the chronicity supports F34.1.
